solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: At heart, racist rotter, a chirpy sort (6)

indicatorNotes.At heart: the heart of a word is its middle letters

blocks.note: the two central letters of raCIst
a cad is a rotter, a dishonourable man
taken as printed

annotation.surface: Someone is being denounced as a bigot and a scoundrel who is annoyingly cheerful.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A chirpy sort' sounds like a description of a cheery person, which is how the insect hides: the cicada is famous for its loud chirping.
annotation.definitionFit: A cicada is an insect whose males produce a loud, persistent chirping song.

entries.clue: Cab owner originally caught in isolated rank (9)

indicatorNotes.originally: the original letters of words are their first ones
indicatorNotes.in: the caught letter goes inside the word for isolated

blocks.note: first letters of Cab and Owner
lonely = isolated; it takes C before its last letter
c = caught, the cricket scoring abbreviation

annotation.surface: A taxi owner has been stranded somewhere remote in a line of cabs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rank' reads as a taxi rank, which the cab supports, but it is military rank: a colonelcy is the office of colonel.
annotation.definitionFit: The -cy suffix names an office or status, as in captaincy, so a colonelcy is one particular military rank.

entries.clue: Several ancient cardinals from the city (5)

blocks.note: 100 in Roman numerals: 'cardinals' are cardinal numbers, 'ancient' makes them Roman
4 in Roman numerals
1 in Roman numerals
100 again

annotation.surface: A group of cardinals from long ago came from the city, perhaps Rome.
annotation.walkthrough: Cardinals look like churchmen, and 'from the city' fits Rome, but they are cardinal numbers written in the ancient Roman style.
annotation.definitionFit: Civic means belonging to or coming from a city.

entries.clue: Capital Radio presenter on current stint before one (8)

blocks.note: a disc jockey
I is the symbol for electric current
a bout is a spell or stint of activity
I = one, the Roman numeral

annotation.surface: A presenter on Capital Radio is doing a current stint before a one o'clock slot.
annotation.walkthrough: Capital Radio is a real London station, so 'Capital' seems part of its name; it is the definition, Djibouti being the capital of Djibouti.
annotation.definitionFit: Djibouti City is the capital of the East African state of Djibouti.

entries.clue: Cherished memory of Dame Melba, for the most part vague (8)

annotation.definitionNote: EMBALMED is an adjective; the phrase stands for 'embalmed in the memory of', i.e. preserved and cherished there

indicatorNotes.for the most part: most of a word is all but its last letter
indicatorNotes.vague: vague letters are indistinct, not in their proper order

blocks.clueFragment: Dame Melba, for the most part
blocks.note: DAME MELBA without its final A

annotation.surface: Someone recalls the soprano Dame Nellie Melba fondly but can barely picture her.
annotation.walkthrough: Dame Nellie Melba was a famous Australian opera singer; the name is only raw letters here.
annotation.definitionFit: Embalming preserves a body from decay; used figuratively, a memory kept fresh and treasured is embalmed.

entries.clue: Growth of bizarre oldish grammar (5,8)

indicatorNotes.bizarre: bizarre letters are in a strange, unexpected order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: Someone notes a rise in odd, old-fashioned grammar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Growth' reads as an increase in usage; here it is a plant growing.
annotation.definitionFit: The marsh marigold is a yellow-flowered plant of wet ground, so a growth in the botanical sense.

entries.clue: Approvingly regard face of murderer in a grave (6)

indicatorNotes.face of: a word's face is its front letter
indicatorNotes.in: 'in a grave' puts the murderer's letter inside the word for grave, as a body lies in a grave

blocks.note: taken as printed
a grave situation is a dire one; it holds M after its D
first letter of Murderer

annotation.surface: Someone gazes with approval at a killer's face lying in a grave.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grave' looks like a burial place in a murder story; it is the adjective meaning serious.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'approvingly' supplies the warmth and 'regard' the looking that admire combines.

entries.clue: Model maiden, one of five flanking former queen (9)

indicatorNotes.flanking: QUIN stands at the side of ANNE

blocks.note: m = maiden, a maiden over in cricket scoring
Queen Anne, who reigned 1702 to 1714
a quin is one of quintuplets

annotation.surface: A model young woman, one of quintuplets, stands beside a former monarch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Model maiden' reads as an exemplary girl; 'Model' alone is the definition, a dummy for displaying clothes.
annotation.definitionFit: A mannequin is a model, either a dummy in a shop window or a person who models clothes.

entries.clue: Half of select military unit packs range of light bedding (5)

indicatorNotes.Half of: take the first half of the word

blocks.note: first half of DETAIL, a small group selected for a duty
ultraviolet, a range of the spectrum; it goes inside DET

annotation.surface: Half of an elite army unit carries a range of lightweight bedding in its kit.
annotation.walkthrough: The split is the trap: 'range of light' is ultraviolet, and 'light bedding' is not the definition. A detail is a squad picked for a task.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a duvet, the continental quilt, is one kind of bedding.

entries.clue: Actors, say, contend to appear in El Jueves every so often (7)

indicatorNotes.to appear in: VIE appears inside the other letters

blocks.note: even letters of eL jUeVeS
to vie is to contend; it goes before the S

annotation.surface: Actors compete to be featured in El Jueves, a Spanish satirical weekly, from time to time.
annotation.walkthrough: Luvvies is British slang, mildly mocking, for actors and theatre people, from their habit of calling each other 'luvvie'.
annotation.definitionFit: Luvvies are actors, especially effusive or pretentious ones; 'say' marks actors as an example.

entries.clue: Terribly hot aftertaste is really quite hot! (5-2-3-3)

indicatorNotes.Terribly: the letters are terribly arranged, ready to be rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: A diner complains that a fiery aftertaste is far too spicy.
annotation.walkthrough: Both 'hot's seem to be about chilli; the second means fashionable and up to date.
annotation.definitionFit: State-of-the-art things are the latest and most advanced, which is what 'hot' means of a gadget.

entries.clue: Dynasty, rejecting outsiders, pushed around sultanate (7)

indicatorNotes.rejecting outsiders: drop the first and last letters
indicatorNotes.around: 'around' in its sense of surrounding: the shortened verb encircles the sultanate

blocks.note: DROVE (pushed, as cattle) without its outer D and E
Oman is a sultanate; it sits between R and OV

annotation.surface: A ruling family, having turned away foreigners, bullied a neighbouring sultanate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outsiders' sounds like foreigners in a political story; it is only the outer letters of the next word.
annotation.definitionFit: The Romanovs were the dynasty that ruled Russia from 1613 to 1917.

entries.clue: On the counter, old tin containing hot snack (5)

indicatorNotes.On the counter: counter means going against the direction, so the letters run backwards
indicatorNotes.containing: the old tin holds H inside it

blocks.note: o = old
h = hot, as on a tap
a tin is a can; with O it holds H, and the whole then runs backwards

annotation.surface: An old tin of something hot sits on a shop counter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the counter' paints a shop or bar, where nachos are served; here it tells you to read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip, usually served with melted cheese as a snack.

entries.clue: Loathsome brother, an eccentric (9)

indicatorNotes.eccentric: eccentric letters are off-centre, out of their normal order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Someone describes their hateful brother as a weirdo.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' looks like a noun describing the brother; it is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Abhorrent means loathsome, inspiring disgust.

entries.clue: Guide had initially tracked changes in latitude (4,3,3)

indicatorNotes.initially: 'initially' means at the start, so only the start of 'tracked' is used
indicatorNotes.changes: 'changes' as a verb: the letters change their order
indicatorNotes.in: the rearranged letters go inside LEEWAY

blocks.note: leeway = latitude, freedom of action; it opens after LE
HAD plus T, first of Tracked, rearranged

annotation.surface: A guide used edit tracking to follow changes in latitude on a journey.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tracked changes' is a word-processing term and 'latitude' a map term, both red herrings. Latitude here is freedom to act, not a line on a map.
annotation.definitionFit: To lead the way is to guide others, going first.

entries.clue: Church holds up a cross on which one might stand? (9)

indicatorNotes.holds up: in a down clue, the church lies below and holds up the letters above it

blocks.note: taken as printed
X is a cross
a minster is a large church, like York Minster

annotation.surface: A church raises a crucifix on a platform for someone to stand on.
annotation.walkthrough: An Axminster is a kind of carpet, named after the Devon town where it was first woven, so it is something one stands on; the question mark flags the indirect definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An Axminster carpet covers a floor, so it is what one might stand on.

entries.clue: Go from Italian city having no time for lunch? (4)

indicatorNotes.having no: a city having no lunchtime is the city's name without the letter that stands for it

blocks.note: Turin, in Piedmont
one o'clock is lunchtime, and one is I; it comes out of TURIN

annotation.surface: Someone leaves Turin because there is no time to stop for lunch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Go' and 'turn' are the same noun, as in 'it's your go'. The question mark flags the stretch from lunchtime to one o'clock to I.
annotation.definitionFit: A go is a turn, as in taking turns at a game.

entries.clue: New school taking on one from Sorbonne and unknown English philosopher (9)

indicatorNotes.taking on: N and SCH take on the middle letters, holding them between
indicatorNotes.from Sorbonne: a word from the Sorbonne is French, so 'and' becomes ET

blocks.note: n = new
I = one, the Roman numeral
et is French for 'and'; the Sorbonne is the Paris university
z is an unknown in algebra
sch = school, the abbreviation
e = English

annotation.surface: A new school hires a Sorbonne academic and an obscure English philosopher.
annotation.walkthrough: 'English philosopher' reads as one phrase, but English is only the final E and the philosopher is German.
annotation.definitionFit: Friedrich Nietzsche was a 19th-century German philosopher.

entries.clue: Assumed wise men should stop in east before ending in yard (8)

indicatorNotes.should stop in: MAGI stop up the word IN, going inside it
indicatorNotes.before: E comes before the last piece
indicatorNotes.ending in: the ending in a word is its final letter, so only the close of 'yard' is used

blocks.note: taken as printed; it holds MAGI
the Magi, the three wise men of the Nativity
e = east
last letter of yarD

annotation.surface: It was assumed the wise men would stop off in the east before finishing their trip in a yard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a preposition joining 'stop' to 'east', but it is the word the Magi go inside.
annotation.definitionFit: Assumed and imagined both mean supposed without proof.

entries.clue: Periodically, revolutionary Tory member’s to make progress with Labour? (4)

indicatorNotes.Periodically: 'periodically' means at regular intervals, so letters are taken at every second position
indicatorNotes.revolutionary: a revolution turns things round, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: even letters of tOrY are OY, turned round
a Member of Parliament

annotation.surface: A radical Conservative MP now and then works with the Labour Party to get things done.
annotation.walkthrough: Yomp is British military slang for a long march carrying heavy kit. The political surface makes 'Labour' the party; it is plain hard labour, capitalised as disguise.
annotation.definitionFit: To yomp is to march laboriously over rough ground, so to make progress with toil.

entries.clue: Nothing at all about resolute article confronting church’s assertion (10)

indicatorNotes.confronting: AN stands face to face with, just before, CE

blocks.note: FA, short for 'sweet FA', slang for nothing at all, turned round
firm = resolute
the indefinite article
the Church of England

annotation.surface: Someone scoffs that a piece claiming to confront the church's position says nothing at all.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' could be containment, but FIRM inside FA gives nothing; here it reverses FA. Sweet FA is British slang for nothing.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though a rare one: affirmance is an older form of affirmation, a declaration that something is true.

entries.clue: Picturesque canals on vacation served up pleasant cycling (6)

indicatorNotes.on vacation: the word is vacated, emptied of its middle
indicatorNotes.served up: in a down clue, up means read bottom to top, so the letters reverse
indicatorNotes.cycling: the last letter cycles round to the front

blocks.note: CanalS emptied, leaving its outer letters; they go upwards
nice = pleasant; its final E moves to the front, giving ENIC

annotation.surface: A holiday by picturesque canals offered some pleasant cycling.
annotation.walkthrough: Holiday canals and cycling paint a tourist brochure; 'vacation' and 'cycling' are both instructions.
annotation.definitionFit: Scenic means picturesque, having fine views.

entries.clue: Personal ID carbon copies taken by state puppet (9)

indicatorNotes.taken by: CC is taken into OHIO, held inside it

blocks.note: a personal identification number
the US state; it takes CC after its O
cc = carbon copies, as on emails

annotation.surface: A state stooge photocopies someone's identity documents.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State puppet' reads as a government stooge; the state is Ohio and the puppet a wooden boy.
annotation.definitionFit: Pinocchio is the wooden puppet of Collodi's story whose nose grows when he lies.

entries.clue: Coat dad wrapped round chest (5)

indicatorNotes.wrapped round: 'wrapped round' as a coat is wrapped round a body: the first word encloses the second

blocks.note: pa = dad
an ark is a chest, as in the Ark of the Covenant; it sits inside PA

annotation.surface: Dad has his coat wrapped round his chest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chest' reads as the body; it is a box, the ark.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the parka, a hooded windproof jacket first made by Arctic peoples, is one kind of coat.

entries.clue: Gaudiness is ugly, essentially obscuring entrance to luxury hotel (5)

indicatorNotes.essentially: the essence of a word is its middle
indicatorNotes.obscuring entrance to: to obscure a building's entrance is to hide its front, so the hotel's first letter disappears

blocks.note: middle letters of uGLy
the RITZ, the London luxury hotel, without its first letter

annotation.surface: Someone complains that showiness is ugly, mostly spoiling the entrance to a grand hotel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Obscuring' sounds like tasteless decor hiding a hotel's doorway; it hides the R of Ritz.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with a tone: glitz is informal for showy, tasteless glamour, which is what gaudiness means.

entries.clue: Lines from sexually adventurous author’s confession? (5)

blocks.note: a confession opens in the first person, the writer saying what they are
bi = bisexual, the informal short form

annotation.surface: A racy writer's memoir contains some revealing lines.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Confession' is the whole of the wordplay: what the author says is I AM BI. The question mark flags this.
annotation.definitionFit: Iambi, plural of iambus, are iambic feet or lines of verse.

entries.clue: Decay picked up below domed building (7)

indicatorNotes.picked up: picked up by the ear, so heard rather than read

blocks.note: rot = decay
UNDA spoken with a non-rhotic British accent is identical to under

annotation.surface: Rot was found underneath a domed building.
annotation.walkthrough: The homophone works only with the British dropped R, where under and 'unda' sound alike.
annotation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building, usually topped by a dome.

entries.clue: Forceful detectives arresting a great number of people from the east (7)

indicatorNotes.arresting: CID holds MANY inside, as police hold a suspect
indicatorNotes.from the east: read from the east, right to left, so backwards

blocks.note: the Criminal Investigation Department
'the many' are a great number of people; it goes inside CID before the whole turns round

annotation.surface: Aggressive detectives are rounding up crowds of people arriving from the east.
annotation.walkthrough: The CID is the British police's plain-clothes detective branch.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: dynamic comes from the Greek for power, and a dynamic person is forceful and full of drive.

entries.clue: Before closure of factory, riot act crushed ruthless behaviour (8)

indicatorNotes.Before: the anagram comes before the Y
indicatorNotes.closure of: the closing letter of the word
indicatorNotes.crushed: crushed letters are squashed out of shape

blocks.note: RIOT ACT rearranged
last letter of factorY

annotation.surface: Before a factory closed, strikers were brutally put down after the Riot Act was read.
annotation.walkthrough: The Riot Act was a British law read aloud to disperse crowds; here RIOT ACT is only letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An atrocity is an act of extreme cruelty, ruthless behaviour.

entries.clue: Without stopping, acted as deputy for counsel (6)

indicatorNotes.Without stopping: stopping is a filling, as in a tooth, so remove the middle

blocks.note: ActeD with its middle letters removed
vice = deputy, as in vice-president

annotation.surface: Someone stood in for a lawyer without a break.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stopping' looks like pausing but means a filling, as in a tooth; 'counsel' looks like a barrister but is guidance.
annotation.definitionFit: Counsel and advice both mean guidance offered to someone.
